scope: Two finite repeats of official MCP SDK 2.3.1 client-generated queue pressure against a checksum-verified, unsigned experimental Debian 12 amd64 package in a route-free fixture namespace. The installed server ran with a 64-descriptor soft limit in a 128 MiB, 64 PID disposable container.
reproduce: Set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR to the pinned npm-installed tools/mcp-sdk-probe directory, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE to the checksum-verified .deb, and OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE_SHA256 to its digest; run bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp twice.
checks: Both runs verified package version and installed executable hash, eight admitted list results, ninth MCP_INPUT_BUSY without a marked HTTP hit, EGRESS_CANCELLED audit and closed socket, approved same-process recovery GET, package uninstall/residue, and no remaining test container or namespace.
sampling: An in-container monitor started while the HTTP fetch was held, sampled /proc/<server-pid>/fd with a 5 ms requested sleep through the burst and recovery, and reported its maximum and count after a stop marker. The server /proc limits showed a 64-descriptor soft limit. The maximum observed value is a sampled lower bound on the actual transient peak; no exact peak or general load bound is claimed.
limitations: A single SDK client and two short bursts on one Debian artifact; no sustained or arbitrary concurrency, other platform, Claude/Codex/Cursor-generated overload, traffic through other tools, exact official candidate, owner acceptance or independent human review is claimed. Container memory and PID high-water marks include fixture setup/helpers; the server VmHWM is process-specific. The four AI Scraping Defense repositories require separate evidence.
